applies_why: The judge is grading a challenge in which the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is a footed chain pressed against Matthew 1:20, so K-C governs the collision.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — I weighed whether using Matthew 1:20's own words is part of chain-vs-chain footing or a forbidden verse-by-verse/stating-verse test.
why: The judge lets Matthew 1:20's own sentence state the source against the challenger's footed analogy, rather than weighing the challenger's chain against the defender's chain by footing.
